key_insight: Dielectric measurements reveal a shift from collective relaxation to localized orientational defects during AESO curing, while machine learning potentials quantify the rotational barriers.
engineering_relevance: Linking rotational energetics to dielectric response could help interpret cure monitoring in bio-based polymer networks.
method: Measure dielectric permittivity at 500–5000 Hz during intermittent UV curing of AESO:VDM with DMPA.
Analyze relaxation dynamics using sliding-window Shannon entropy and Grassberger–Procaccia correlation integrals.
Benchmark MACE-OFF23 relaxed dihedral scans of five AESO-fragment rotational modes against DFT.
evidence_signal: MACE reproduces all five DFT profile shapes with Pearson r = 0.95–0.98 and preserves the barrier hierarchy; Arrhenius estimates place acrylate rotations closest to the dielectric frequency window.
watch_item: MACE underestimates barriers by 3–20%, and fragment-based Arrhenius estimates do not directly validate rotational rates in the curing network.
paper_title: Machine learning interatomic potentials and orientational defects in polymers
